headline: RBA holds rates steady but warns another hike is still on the table — while PLS surged 2.75% on the ASX and US tech slipped last night.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a strong session today, up 2.75% to $6.36. The move comes as spodumene (the lithium ore Pilbara mines) prices show early signs of tightening, with analysts watching whether ASX lithium stocks can sustain a recovery. It's a positive sign but still early days — PLS is still in the red overall at -5.64% on your total investment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell 2.11% last night to $385.52. No major single catalyst — the broader NASDAQ was flat, so this looks like sector rotation or profit-taking after a strong run. MSFT is now down 13% on your total investment, making it the biggest drag in the portfolio.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 1.94% last night to $363.89, moving in line with the broader soft tone for big tech. Analysts still have upside price targets flagged, so this looks like a routine pullback rather than anything fundamentally new. You're still up 18.36% on your total GOOG investment.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped 0.72% today to $17.94. The ETF tracks global AI companies, and with MSFT and GOOG both soft last night, that weakness flowed through to today's ASX session. Still sitting 5% below your cost base overall.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 0.84% today to $8.22. The IEA (International Energy Agency) released a report flagging a significant oil surplus expected in 2027 as the Strait of Hormuz situation eases and demand destruction from the Iran conflict bites. Lower oil prices are bad for energy company earnings, which flows through to this ETF.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.39% today to $77.55 — a small but solid gain. As a diversified fund across global shares and bonds, it benefited from the mix of the ASX holding up and gold prices rising. Now up 2.88% on your total investment.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped a modest 0.39% today to $94.37. Emerging markets were fairly quiet — no major catalyst. Essentially flat on your total investment at -0.23%.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.27% today to $526.75, reflecting the mild US market softness from last night. Still up 2.14% on your total investment overall.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped just 0.54% last night to $228.73, holding up relatively well. GTA 6 buzz is building — Piper Sandler recently weighed in positively on GTA VI's commercial prospects, and the Take-Two CEO hinted at pricing. Gamers are circling 23 June on their calendars for what looks like a major announcement.

watch_today.title: RBA holds at 4.35% — but warns rates could go higher
watch_today.detail: The RBA kept the cash rate on hold at 4.35% this week, which is welcome relief for mortgage holders. But the nine words nobody wanted to hear: the RBA explicitly said it's 'not ruling out' another rate hike if inflation stays stubborn. A Middle East ceasefire reduces oil price pressure, but the RBA isn't ready to declare victory yet. Watch for any inflation data prints over coming weeks.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Pilbara Minerals bouncing on lithium price signals
watch_today.detail: PLS jumped 2.75% today to $6.36. Analysts are watching spodumene (lithium ore) prices for signs of a sustained recovery — a few recent articles suggest tightening supply and restart discipline among producers could support prices. You're still down 5.64% overall, but this is the most encouraging session in a while. Worth holding to see if the momentum continues.

watch_today.title: MSFT — biggest portfolio drag after another soft night
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 2.11% last night to $385.52 and is now 13% below your cost base — that's the largest dollar loss in the portfolio at -$51 AUD. There's no major fundamental break, but the stock has been drifting. Unless you see a clear catalyst (earnings, major product news), holding makes sense — selling now risks locking in the loss just before a potential recovery.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 news heating up, 23 June circled
watch_today.detail: Take-Two held up well last night (-0.54%). The GTA 6 hype machine is running: the Take-Two CEO has hinted at pricing (potentially above the usual $70 USD), Piper Sandler analysts recently upgraded their view on GTA VI's commercial potential causing a 6% jump earlier, and gaming fans are pointing to 23 June for a major update. This is a genuine near-term catalyst for TTWO — worth watching closely this week.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — oil outlook darkening, IEA flags 2027 glut
watch_today.detail: The IEA (International Energy Agency) cut its 2026 oil demand forecast today and now sees a significant oil surplus in 2027 as the Strait of Hormuz reopens and demand destruction from the Iran conflict plays out. WTI crude slipped to $75.44 last night. This is a headwind for FUEL.AX, which holds global energy companies whose earnings track oil prices. Keep an eye on whether oil stabilises or keeps falling.

watch_today.title: Gold hits $4,398 — tailwind for diversified holdings
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 1.55% last night to $4,398 USD/oz — a strong move. Gold rising typically signals investors are nervous and seeking safety, which can also support your VDHG holding (which has a bond component). It's also a reminder that global uncertainty (Middle East, AI regulation debates) hasn't gone away despite the ceasefire.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was basically flat — the S&P 500 barely moved (+0.003%) and the NASDAQ crept up just 0.11%, even though individual big-tech names like MSFT and GOOG had a rough night. Gold was the standout, jumping 1.55% to $4,398/oz as investors sought safety. Oil slipped to $75.44 as the IEA flagged a looming global supply glut. The Aussie dollar is sitting steady at 70.77 US cents. ASX 200 data wasn't available for today's close, but individual ASX holdings showed mixed action — PLS the clear winner, energy and AI ETFs under mild pressure.

politics.summary: The RBA dominated domestic news this week, holding rates at 4.35% but refusing to rule out further hikes. The central bank is watching inflation closely and isn't popping the champagne just yet — even with a Middle East ceasefire reducing some price pressures.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rate at 4.35% but warns another hike is still possible
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia kept the official cash rate at 4.35% this week — no cut, no hike. That means your mortgage repayments stay the same for now, which is a relief. But the RBA used nine words that made borrowers nervous: it said it's 'not ruling out' another rate hike if inflation doesn't keep falling. A ceasefire in the Middle East removes some oil-driven inflation pressure, but the RBA wants to see more evidence before it relaxes. If you're on a variable rate mortgage, don't expect relief anytime soon.

stories.title: Guardian analysis: Why the RBA is cautious despite the Middle East ceasefire
stories.why_it_matters: Even though a Middle East peace deal eases oil prices — which helps inflation — the Guardian notes the RBA is still cautious because domestic services inflation (things like rent, insurance, and dining out) remains sticky. The RBA's concern is that cutting rates too early could re-ignite price pressures. Expect the rate to stay on hold for several more months before any cut becomes realistic.

ai.summary: AI governance was the big theme today — tech CEOs were at the G7 alongside world leaders, Trump's political fight with Anthropic is raising alarm bells about US AI dominance, and a leading AI scientist is asking whether it'll take a catastrophe before governments act.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google CEOs join Trump and world leaders at G7 summit
stories.why_it_matters: For the first time, the heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google sat at the table with G7 world leaders — a clear signal that AI companies now carry geopolitical weight once reserved for heads of state. CNBC described it as 'a signal of where power sits.' This means AI governance is now a top-tier international issue, not just a tech industry conversation. For investors in GOOG and GXAI, it confirms AI is being treated as critical national infrastructure — which cuts both ways (more regulation risk, but also more government support).

stories.title: Trump's war on Anthropic threatens America's AI dominance
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration's political targeting of Anthropic — one of the leading US AI labs and a rival to OpenAI — is being called a threat to America's ability to stay ahead of China in AI. The concern is that regulatory and political pressure could push AI talent and investment offshore. For your GXAI.AX holding (which tracks global AI companies including US leaders), prolonged political uncertainty around AI funding and regulation is a risk worth watching.

stories.title: Will it take a 'Chernobyl-scale disaster' to get AI regulated? — Stuart Russell, Guardian
stories.why_it_matters: Stuart Russell, one of the world's most respected AI researchers, argues in The Guardian that governments are moving too slowly on AI safety — and that it might take a major catastrophe before real regulation arrives, similar to how Chernobyl prompted nuclear safety overhauls. He's calling for binding international agreements. This is the kind of longer-term systemic risk that AI-focused investors (GXAI, GOOG) should keep on their radar — heavy-handed regulation after a crisis event could reshape the sector fast.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 kicks off Friday night, with injury news filtering through today. The Gold Coast Titans host the Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday at 5:30pm — circle that one. AFL team tips are also out with some big outs for this weekend's games.

stories.title: NRL Casualty Ward: Tom Trbojevic back on deck; Nicho Hynes and Andrew Brailey in frame for return
stories.why_it_matters: Good news for the Sea Eagles: 'Turbo' Tom Trbojevic appears on track to return after injury, which is a massive boost given he's one of the competition's best. Sharks halfback Nicho Hynes and hooker Andrew Brailey are also in frame to come back this round — key players for Cronulla as they push for a top-four spot. Bulldogs vs Sea Eagles is Saturday night at Accor Stadium, so Turbo's availability is the big question heading in.

stories.title: Titans vs Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium — Saturday 5:30pm
stories.why_it_matters: Your local team the Gold Coast Titans host the back-to-back premiers Penrith Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium this Saturday at 5:30pm. Round 16 team lists are confirmed — check the NRL draw for confirmed lineups. The Panthers are always dangerous but the Titans at home in a local Gold Coast match is always worth a watch.

stories.title: Gold Coast Suns cop big fine after fifth umpire contact incident this season
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Suns have been fined by the AFL for a fifth umpire contact incident this season — that's a notable pattern that suggests a culture or discipline issue creeping in at the club. Repeated fines and suspensions hurt team depth. This is their fifth offence, so the fines are escalating. Not ideal timing heading into the business end of the season.

stories.title: Williams sisters team up for first time in 10 years ahead of Wimbledon
stories.why_it_matters: Serena and Venus Williams are reportedly teaming up for doubles at Wimbledon — their first partnership in a decade. Wimbledon is just around the corner, and the Williams sisters' return as a duo would be one of the most watched storylines of the tournament. No confirmation yet on wildcards or draw placement, but it's generating plenty of buzz ahead of the grass-court Grand Slam.
